100.description: Pesticides targeting insects, but have low toxicity or low potential for human exposure, applied by professionally licensed exterminators and maintenance staff.
100.name: Commercial use of "Best Practice" products

101.description: Tetralogy of Fallot is a congenital heart defect that affects how blood flows through the heart.
101.name: Tetralogy of Fallot

102.description: Pesticides targeting rats and mice, applied by professional exterminators or licensed maintenance staff. These products are frequently added to tamper proof containers or applied directly to rodent burrows.
102.name: Commercial use of rodenticides

103.description: Households with incomes below the federal poverty level. Households without sufficient resources are often deprived of access to health care, good quality housing, and other resources that protect health.
103.name: Neighborhood poverty

107.description: The presence of cockroaches in the home is often associated with poor housing maintenance. Cockroaches in the home can contaminate food and worsen asthma.
107.name: Homes with cockroaches

14.description: People born outside the USA or its territories (including Puerto Rico).
14.name: Foreign-born population

15.description: Households with more than one person per room.
15.name: Household crowding

16.description: Homes built before 1950. Older housing can put residents at risk of lead poisoning.
16.name: Very old homes

17.description: Housing units occupied by their owner.
17.name: Owner-occupied homes

18.description: Adults reporting an asthma diagnosis, and symptoms, in the last 12 months (from when they were surveyed). Poor air quality and housing issues increase risk of developing and triggering asthma.
18.name: Adults with a recent asthma attack

2017.description: Adults without a smoke-free home policy. A smoke-free home policy can limit people's exposure to secondhand smoke, which is especially dangerous to children.
2017.name: No smoke-free home policy

2019.description: Adults who are current smokers. Cigarette smoking is the leading cause of preventable deaths in the USA. It causes many diseases and greatly harms health.
2019.name: Cigarette smoking (adults)

2020.description: Adults reporting secondhand smoke at work. Secondhand smoke, especially indoors, is bad for health.
2020.name: Secondhand smoke at work

2021.description: High school students who smoked in the past 30 days (from when they were surveyed). Cigarette smoking is the leading cause of preventable deaths in the USA. It causes many diseases and greatly harms health.
2021.name: Cigarette smoking (youth)

2023.description: Concentration of fine particles in the air. Fine particles are emitted by vehicles, building boilers, and other combustion — and are a major form of air pollution that harms health. Neighborhood sensors measure PM2.5 at the street-level, where people are most active. These sensors are designed to let us measure differences in air pollution over time and locations within New York City.
2023.name: Fine particles (PM 2.5)

2024.description: Concentration of black carbon in the air. Black carbon is a major component of fine particles, which contribute to both short-term health effects and chronic illness
2024.name: Black carbon

2025.description: Concentration of nitrogen dioxide in the air. Nitrogen dioxide is a pollutant formed by combustion. It causes breathing problems and contributes to smog and acid rain.
2025.name: Nitrogen dioxide (NO2)

2026.description: Concentration of sulfur dioxide in the air. Sulfur dioxide comes from burning some kinds of fuel oil. It can worsen lung diseases.
2026.name: Sulfur dioxide (SO2)

2027.description: Concentration of ozone in the air. Ozone is a common air pollutant that can harm breathing and worsen respiratory conditions.
2027.name: Ozone (O3)

2028.description: Concentration of nitric oxide in the air. Nitric oxide is formed by combusion, causes breathing problems, and contributes to smog and acid rain.
2028.name: Nitric oxide (NO)

2030.description: Adults reporting bed bugs that required an exterminator, in the past 12 months (from when they were surveyed).
2030.name: Bed bugs

2033.description: Cancers that start in the brain or spinal cord.
2033.name: Brain and other nervous system cancer (children)

2035.description: A cancer of the blood and bone marrow.
2035.name: Acute myeloid leukemia (children)

2037.description: A cancer of the blood and bone marrow.
2037.name: Acute lymphocytic leukemia (children)

2039.description: A group of diseases where cells grow abnormally.
2039.name: All cancer (children)

2041.description: Concentration of nitrate in drinking water. Nitrates are found in water near where nitrogen-based fertilizers are used. Infants who are fed formula made with water containing nitrates over 10 mg/L sometimes became seriously ill.
2041.name: Nitrate

2043.description: Concentration of total trihalomethane in drinking water. Disinfection by-products are chemicals that form when a disinfectant like chlorine reacts with naturally occurring organic matter and other substances in the source water. Current research is investigating whether there are health effects from chronic exposure to the by-products of water disinfection.
2043.name: Disinfection by-products (HAA5)

2044.description: Concentration of arsenic in drinking water. Arsenic occurrs naturally in some groundwater systems. It may also enter drinking water systems from some pesticides and wood preservatives. Chronic exposure may increase risk of certain cancers.
2044.name: Arsenic

2048.description: Severe asthma attacks can result in a visit to the ED. Things like smoke, air pollution, dust mites, cockroaches, mold, pollen and pet dander can trigger asthma.
2048.name: Asthma emergency department visits (age 4 and under)

2049.description: Places with licenses to sell alcohol. Greater alcohol outlet density has been associated with a variety of health effects.
2049.name: Alcohol access

2050.description: Adults who reported having more than 2 drinks per day (men) or more than 1 drink per day ( women).
2050.name: Heavy drinking (adults)

2051.description: Adults who reported having 5 or more drinks on one occasion, and as of 2011, 4 or more drinks for women, in the past 30 days (from when they were surveyed).
2051.name: Binge drinking (adults)

2055.description: Public high school students who reported having 5 or more drinks in a row in the past 30 days (from when they were surveyed).
2055.name: Binge drinking (youth)

2056.description: Public high school students who report having at least 1 drink in the past 30 days (from when they were surveyed).
2056.name: Underage drinking

2057.description: Places with licenses to sell alcohol, by youth population. Greater alcohol outlet density is associated with a variety of health effects.
2057.name: Alcohol access (youth)

2058.description: Adults reporting walking or biking for transportation in the last 30 days (from when they were surveyed). Regularly walking or biking for transportation is good for you.
2058.name: Walking or biking for transportation

2059.description: Adults reporting having ridden a bicycle at least once a month in the past year.
2059.name: Monthly bicycle use

2060.description: Adults reporting exercise in the past 30 days (from when they were surveyed). Regular exercise is a key way to stay healthy.
2060.name: Recent exercise

2061.description: Adults reporting a Body Mass Index over 25. People who are overweight or obese are at increased risk for heart disease and diabetes.  Neighborhood factors such as walkability and the types of food retail outlets available can impact residents' risk of being overweight or obese.
2061.name: Overweight or obesity (adults)

2062.description: Youths reporting a Body Mass Index over 25. People who are overweight or obese are at increased risk for heart disease and diabetes.  Neighborhood factors such as walkability and the types of food retail outlets available can impact residents' risk of being overweight or obese.
2062.name: Overweight or obesity (youth)

2063.description: Adults reporting a Body Mass Index over 30. People who are overweight or obese are at increased risk for heart disease and diabetes.  Neighborhood factors such as walkability and the types of food retail outlets available can impact residents' risk of being overweight or obese.
2063.name: Obesity (adults)

2064.description: Youths reporting a Body Mass Index over 30. People who are overweight or obese are at increased risk for heart disease and diabetes.  Neighborhood factors such as walkability and the types of food retail outlets available can impact residents' risk of being overweight or obese.
2064.name: Obesity (youth)

2065.description: An A grade is the highest a restaurant can score in a health inspection. It indicates a well maintained restaurant with clean and safe food handling and storage practices, minimizing the risk of food poisoning.
2065.name: Restaurants with A grades

2073.description: Adults reporting their neighborhood is safe from crime. Whether people perceive their neighborhood as safe can affect whether they will spend time outside, use parks, and use active and sustainable forms of transportation. It can also affect mental well-being.
2073.name: Perception of neighborhood safety

2074.description: Deaths directly attributed to heat, according to death certificates. Hot weather kills more people than all other extreme weather combined. This measure represents a small proportion of all heat-related deaths.
2074.name: Heat stress: deaths

2075.description: ED visits due to heat-related illnesses, such as heat stroke and heat exhaustion. These represent part of the public health burden of extreme heat.
2075.name: Heat stress: yearly emergency department visits

2076.description: Hospitalizations due to heat stress. These are part of the public health burden of hot weather.
2076.name: Heat stress: yearly hospitalizations

2077.description: Esophageal cancer forms in the tissues of the esophagus, in the throat.
2077.name: Esophageal cancer

2084.description: Days over 90 degrees. More people die due to extreme heat than all other extreme weather events combined. As the climate continues to warm, we can expect more severe and more frequent heat events.
2084.name: Heat events

2086.description: Nonfatal hospitalizations due to bicycle injuries. Bicycle injury hospitalizations can indicate the overall safety of cycling in the city.
2086.name: Bicycle injury hospitalizations

2087.description: Kidney and renal pelvis cancers start in the kidney.
2087.name: Kidney and renal pelvis cancer

2088.description: Larynx cancer starts in the tissues of the larynx.
2088.name: Larynx cancer

2089.description: Cancers of the liver and intrahepatic bile duct.
2089.name: Liver and intrahepatic bile duct cancer

2090.description: A dangerous form of skin cancer.
2090.name: Melanoma of the skin

2091.description: Cancers of the mouth and throat.
2091.name: Oral cavity and pharynx cancer

2092.description: ED visits related to bicycle injuries.  Bicycle injury ED visits can indicate the overall safety of cycling in the city.
2092.name: Bicycle injury emergency department visits

2093.description: Nonfatal transportation-related hospitalizations to pedestrians. Pedestrian injury hospitalizations can indicate the safety of walking for transportation.
2093.name: Pedestrian injury hospitalizations

2094.description: Transportation-related ED visits for pedestrians. Pedestrian injury ED visits can indicate the safety of walking for transportation.
2094.name: Pedestrian injury emergency department visits

2095.description: A cancer caused by exposure to asbestos.
2095.name: Mesothelioma

2096.description: Bladder cancer is a common type of cancer. It typically affects older adults.
2096.name: Bladder cancer

2097.description: Adults reporting that they drink 1 or more sugary drinks per day. Sugary drinks contribute to an unhealthy, high-calorie diet.
2097.name: Sugary drink consumption (adults)

2098.description: Youths reporting that they drink 1 or more sugary drinks per day. Sugary drinks contribute to an unhealthy, high-calorie diet.
2098.name: Sugary drink consumption (youth)

2101.description: Adults reporting mold in the home. Mold can worsen respiratory conditions like asthma, and indicate housing problems in a building.
2101.name: Mold in homes

2104.description: Adults reporting having an air conditioner. Air conditioning reduces the risk of heat stroke and other heat-related illness.
2104.name: Adults with air conditioners

2105.description: Mice and rats are a source of household allergens connected to developing or worsening asthma.
2105.name: Adults reporting mice or rats inside

2108.description: Estimated annual deaths due to PM2.5 air pollution. Estimating these deaths is a way to understand how air pollution increases mortality.
2108.name: Deaths due to PM2.5

2112.description: Annual vehicle miles travelled. Traffic density can influence health as a source of air pollution and traffic-related injuries.
2112.name: Traffic density

2113.description: Annual vehicle miles travelled by cars. Traffic density can influence health as a source of air pollution and traffic-related injuries.
2113.name: Traffic density (cars)

2114.description: Annual vehicle miles travelled by trucks. Traffic density can influence health as a source of air pollution and traffic-related injuries.
2114.name: Traffic density (trucks)

2117.description: ED visits for asthma due to PM2.5 air pollution. These represent part of the health burden of air pollution.
2117.name: Asthma emergency department visits due to PM2.5

2119.description: Hospitalizations for respiratory issues due to PM2.5 pollution (among people over age 20). These represent part of the health burden of air pollution.
2119.name: Respiratory hospitalizations due to PM2.5 (age 20+)

2120.description: Hospitalizations for cardiovascular issues due to PM2.5 (among people over age 40). These represent part of the health burden of air pollution.
2120.name: Cardiovascular hospitalizations due to PM2.5 (age 40+)

2121.description: Deaths due to cardiac or respiratory issues linked to ozone. These show how air pollution increases mortality.
2121.name: Cardiac and respiratory deaths due to Ozone

2122.description: ED visits for asthma due to ozone. These are part of the health burden of air pollution.
2122.name: Asthma emergency department visits due to Ozone

2124.description: Hospitalizations for asthma due to ozone. These are part of the health burden of air pollution.
2124.name: Asthma hospitalizations due to Ozone

2132.description: Adults with any kind of health insurance. People with health insurance are more likely to have a regular doctor, receive preventive care services, better manage chronic health conditions, and have longer life expectancy.
2132.name: Health insurance (adults)

2133.description: A score that summarizes features that promote walking. These include density of residences, intersections, subway stops, and retail area. Higher scores indicate greater walkability. Neighborhoods range from -4.0 to 9.4, with zero as an approximate NYC average. This indicator excludes some factors that may impact access and walkability, like maintenance, ADA access, neighborhood safety, and street trees.
2133.name: Walkability index

2135.description: ED visits due to falls among people over age 65. Falls are a leading cause of injury among older adults.
2135.name: Fall-related emergency department visits (age 65+)

2136.description: Hospitalizations due to falls among people over age 65. Falls are a leading cause of injury among older adults.
2136.name: Fall-related hospitalizations (age 65+)

2140.description: Hurricane Evacuation Zones are determined by New York City Emergency Management and indicate varying threat levels of coastal flooding from storm surge. Evacuation orders may be given during hurricanes or coastal flooding events. There are six zones, ranked by storm surge risk. Zone 1 is the highest risk for flooding. Residents in these zones may receive evacuation orders during hurricanes or tropical storms.
2140.name: Residents living in a hurricane evacuation zone

2141.description: Spatial average of surface temperature, measured by satellite. Surface temperatures vary because of vegetative cover (which promotes cooling), and paved roads, sidewalks, and buildings (which retain heat). Hotter neighborhoods tend to have more heat-exacerbated deaths associated with extreme heat events.
2141.name: Daytime summer surface temperature

2143.description: Land covered by trees, grass, or other plants. Vegetative cover reduces temperatures in the immediate area, and may increase air quality.
2143.name: Vegetative cover

2145.description: Adults reporting independent living difficulty due to a physical, mental, or emotional problem. People with disabilities may need additional support during extreme weather. For example, extra planning for safe travel out of evacuation zones during a hurricane, or back-up electricity to support medical equipment during power outages.
2145.name: Independent living difficulty (adults)

2146.description: People age 65+ living alone. People living alone may have more difficulty getting resources they need in an emergency, and are at higher risk of weather-related illnesses like heat stroke and hypothermia.
2146.name: Older adults living alone (65+)

2151.description: Adults who report having a personal doctor. Having a regular doctor makes it easier to maintain good health.
2151.name: Adults with a personal doctor

2155.description: Older adults (over 65) are more vulnerable to hot weather and heat stress. Air conditioning reduces the risk of heat stroke and other heat-related illness.
2155.name: Older adults with air conditioners (age 65+)

2157.description: The percent of a neighborhood that is shaded by trees. Tree shade can lower a neighborhood's temperature, making it more comfortable for physical activity.
2157.name: Tree canopy cover

2158.description: Subway stations per square kilometer. Neighborhoods with greater subway access encourage active transportation, which may increase physical activity and overall health of residents. They also tend to have more foot traffic, which attracts businesses and can foster community.
2158.name: Subway station density

2168.description: Carbon monoxide incidents when there was no alarm. Carbon monoxide detectors are required in NYC homes by law. Failure to provide or maintain a detector can put people at risk for carbon monoxide poisoning and death.
2168.name: Carbon monoxide incidents (without a detector)

2169.description: Diabetes is a metabolic disorder that affects how well your body can get energy from food and drink. Adults can be born with diabetes or develop it later in life. Health problems from diabetes can include heart disease, stroke, vision problems, and amputations.
2169.name: Diabetes (adults)

2172.description: Adults reporting walking for transportation in the last 7 days (from when they were surveyed)
2172.name: Recent walking

2173.description: Adults reporting biking for transportation in the last 7 days (from when they were surveyed).
2173.name: Recent biking

2174.description: Hospitalizations for cold-related illnesses, such as hypothermia and frostbite. These are part of the health burden of cold weather. Cold weather can also make chronic conditions worse.
2174.name: Cold stress: hospitalizations

2175.description: ED visits for cold-related illnesses, such as hypothermia and frostbite. These are part of the health burden of cold weather. Cold weather can also make chronic conditions worse.
2175.name: Cold stress: emergency department visits

2176.description: Children living in households in poverty. Poverty deprives people of access to health and safety resources.
2176.name: Child poverty (under age 5)

2179.description: Renter-occupied homes reporting no housing problems. Healthy homes are free of housing problems.
2179.name: Renter-occupied homes with no housing problems

2181.description: Sidewalk area percentage. Sidewalks are important for commuting, businesses, and physical activity. More sidewalk area contributes to a safer pedestrian environment, supports vibrant business districts and can foster social interaction.
2181.name: Sidewalk area

2184.description: Blood lead levels above 5 mcg/dL among children under age 6. Lead poisoning can cause learning and behavior problems, and delay growth and mental development. There is no safe level of lead in the blood.
2184.name: Elevated blood lead levels (under age 6)

2185.description: Households reporting functioning air conditioning (AC). AC is an important way to prevent heat stress, especially for people with limited mobility.
2185.name: Household air conditioning

2189.description: Children tested for lead before age 3. In New York State, all children must be tested for lead before age 3. There is no safe level of lead in the blood.
2189.name: Lead testing (by age 3)

2191.description: The risk of community-level heat impacts like deaths due to extreme heat events. The HVI is made from data on surface temperature, green space, air conditioning access, median income, and Black population (the population most excluded from heat resources). Differences in community-level heat impacts stem from structural racism, which limits access to preventive resources.
2191.name: Heat vulnerability index

22.description: Adults reporting cockroaches in the past 30 days (from when they were surveyed). Cockroaches are an allergen and can trigger asthma.
22.name: Adults reporting cockroaches

2207.description: Concentration of TTHM in drinking water. Disinfection by-products form when a disinfectant such as chlorine reacts with naturally occurring organic matter in the source water. Current research is investigating whether there are health effects from chronic exposure to the by-products of water disinfection.
2207.name: Disinfection by-products (TTHM)

2208.description: Hospitalizations for asbestosis. Asbestos is a naturally-occurring mineral which was commonly used as an insulation material until the 1970s. Inhaling asbestos fibers can result in the chronic lung disease called asbestosis, a type of pneumoconiosis. New York City construction, insulation, and shipyard workers who installed, disturbed, or removed asbestos without respiratory protection are at risk. Typically it takes more than ten years before symptoms develop. The use of proper protective masks is key to preventing the disease, since there is no treatment.
2208.name: Asbestosis hospitalizations

2209.description: Blood lead levels over 10 mg/dL among people age 16+. In New York City, the most common cause of lead poisoning in non-pregnant adults is from working in the construction. Workers are exposed through lead dust or fumes during work that disturbs old lead paint. Workers in other industries, as well as hobbyists, may be at risk if they work with lead-containing metal, paint, pigments, ceramic glazes or bullets. Adults can also be exposed to lead through lead-contaminated products, like some imported health remedies, spices, foods, pottery and cosmetics.
2209.name: Elevated blood lead levels (age 16+)

2210.description: Hospitalizations for pneumoconiosis, a lung disease caused by breathing in certain particles or fibers over a prolonged period. Pneumoconiosis usually results from a workplace exposure. The most common causes of pneumoconiosis include asbestos fibers, silica dust, and coal dust. There is no cure, but it can be prevented with appropriate respiratory protection.
2210.name: Pneumoconiosis hospitalizations

2211.description: Hospitalizations billed to workers' compensation. Workers' compensation provides medical care for workers injured or become ill as a direct result of their job. Hospitalizations billed to workers' comp represent only a portion of work-related injuries that require hospital care. Workers' compensation policies vary from state-to-state.
2211.name: Hospitalizations billed to workers' compensation

2214.description: Fatal, work-related injuries. These include deaths resulting from unintentional injuries such as falls, acute poisonings, and motor vehicle crashes that occur during travel for work, and intentional injuries (i.e., homicides and suicides) that occur at work.
2214.name: Work-related deaths (all industries)

2215.description: Construction is the most dangerous industry in NYC, with nearly a third of work-related injury deaths each year. Falls from scaffolds, ladders and roofs are the most common cause of fatal injuries among construction workers.
2215.name: Work-related deaths (construction industry), Citywide

2216.description: Elevated blood lead levels are 5+ mcg/dL. There is no safe level of lead in the blood. Lead poisoning can cause learning and behavior problems, and delay growth and mental development.
2216.name: Elevated blood lead levels (under age 6), by NTA

2218.description: Babesiosis is a rare, sometimes severe or fatal tick-borne disease caused by a parasite that infects red blood cells. Babesiosis is transmitted by the bite of an infected blacklegged tick (the same tick that transmits Lyme disease and anaplasmosis). Most patients acquire this disease while traveling outside NYC. However, there has been an increase in the number of cases with no history of travel to endemic areas, primarily in Staten Island, as well as isolated cases in the Bronx and Queens. Babesiosis can also be transmitted through transfused blood products.
2218.name: Babesiosis

2232.description: Adults reporting that their health is excellent, very good, or good.
2232.name: Self-reported health

2235.description: Adults reporting pesticide use in the home. This does not include pesticide applications by professional exterminators.
2235.name: Adults reporting personal use of pesticides

2236.description: Adults reporting driving in the last 30 days (from when they were surveyed).
2236.name: Recent driving

2237.description: Adults reporting messaging while driving in the past 30 days (from when they were surveyed).
2237.name: Recent messaging while driving

2238.description: Adults reporting speeding while driving in the past 30 days (from when they were surveyed).
2238.name: Recent speeding

2239.description: Construction is the most dangerous industry in NYC, with nearly a third of work-related injury deaths each year.
2239.name: Work-related deaths (construction industry), by borough

2312.description: Pest control services provided by a professional exterminator in the individual's home.
2312.name: Commercial insecticide use (by chemical type)

2317.description: Adults incarcerated in NYC facilities. Each component of the criminal justice continuum - from arrest to re-entry - carries various health consequences, and a growing body of literature has documented severe adverse health outcomes for the individual, their families, and neighborhoods.
2317.name: Jail incarceration

2322.description: Deaths before age 65. This can indicate the overall health of a population.
2322.name: Premature mortality

2323.description: Students missing 20 or more school days per year.
2323.name: School absenteeism

2325.description: Population by Census race/ethnicity category. Past and present structural racism has inequitably distributed resources that people need to stay healthy - like job opportunities, healthy housing, high-quality education, and health care.
2325.name: Race and ethnicity

2334.description: People age 25 years and over who have completed high school or high school equivalency.
2334.name: Graduated high school

2335.description: People who do not speak English at home and/or are not English proficient.
2335.name: Limited English

2336.description: Renter households spending 30% of their income or more on rent.
2336.name: Rent-burdened households

2338.description: Adults reporting secondhand smoke at home, from outside sources. Secondhand smoke, especially indoors, is bad for health - especially for the health of children.
2338.name: Secondhand smoke at home (from outside sources)

2339.description: Public high school students who reported having an asthma attack in the past 12 months from when they were surveyed.
2339.name: Youth with a recent asthma attack

2340.description: West Nile virus is transmitted through the bite of infected mosquitoes. While most people who are infected will not go on to develop symptoms, about 20% experience mild or moderate illness and more rarely, neuroinvasive disease which can present as encephalitis or meningitis. Most of the West Nile disease cases detected by the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene represent neuroinvasive disease as these patients are more likely to seek care.
2340.name: West Nile virus

2364.description: Pesticides targeting fungus such as mold or plant blight, applied by NYC agency-contracted exterminators or NYC agency pest control staff. These are often applied to protect landscaping and golf course grasses.
2364.name: NYC agency use of fungicides

2365.description: Court-ordered evictions. Eviction often leads to residential instability, moving into poor quality housing, overcrowding, and homelessness, all of which is associated with negative health among adults and children. People who are threatened with eviction, even before they lose their home, are more likely to report poor health.
2365.name: Evictions (court-ordered)

2366.description: Pesticides targeting insects that are effective, but have low toxicity or low potential for human exposure to humans, applied by NYC agency-contracted exterminators or NYC agency pest control staff.
2366.name: NYC agency use of "Best Practice" products

2367.description: Herbicide containing the chemical glyphosate, targeting unwanted weeds, grasses, vines and trees, applied by NYC agency-contracted exterminators or NYC agency pest control staff. This chemical is often sold commercially as "Roundup".
2367.name: NYC agency use of glyphosate

2368.description: Pesticides targeting unwanted weeds, grasses, vines and trees, applied by NYC agency-contracted exterminators or NYC agency pest control staff.
2368.name: NYC agency use of herbicides

2369.description: Pesticides targeting insects, applied by NYC agency-contracted exterminators or NYC agency pest control staff.
2369.name: NYC agency use of insecticides

2370.description: Pesticides targeting rats and mice, applied by NYC agency-contracted exterminators or NYC agency pest control staff.
2370.name: NYC agency use of rodenticides

2374.description: Pesticides targeting mosquitoes, applied by NYC agency-contracted exterminators or NYC agency pest control staff. These application include treatment of standing water with larvicides and the spraying of adult mosquito infestations.
2374.name: NYC agency use of mosquito control

2375.description: Non-fatal, violence-related injuries that result in hospitalizations. These are more common than homicides and help paint the larger picture of the burden of violence on communities.
2375.name: Violence-related hospitalizations (all ages)

2376.description: Deaths due to cold weather. These are part of the health burden of cold weather. Cold weather can also worsen chronic conditions, sometimes leading to death. This data only includes deaths directly attributed to cold on death certificates.
2376.name: Cold stress: deaths

2377.description: Households with someone using electric medical equipment. People who use electric medical equipment are more vulnerable during power outages or evacuations.
2377.name: Households using electric medical equipment

2378.description: Emergency department visits for asthma. Things like smoke, air pollution, dust mites, cockroaches, mold, pollen and pet dander can trigger asthma.
2378.name: Asthma emergency department visits (age 4 and under), by NTA

2379.description: Emergency department visits for asthma. Things like smoke, air pollution, dust mites, cockroaches, mold, pollen and pet dander can trigger asthma.
2379.name: Asthma emergency department visits (age 5 to 17)

2380.description: Emergency department visits for asthma. Things like smoke, air pollution, dust mites, cockroaches, mold, pollen and pet dander can trigger asthma.
2380.name: Asthma emergency department visits (adults)

2381.description: Hospitalizations for asthma. These more severe asthma outcomes are often clustered in high-poverty neighborhoods, where disinvestment and poor housing conditions expose residents to triggers.
2381.name: Asthma hospitalizations (age 5 to 17)

2382.description: Hospitalizations for asthma. These more severe asthma outcomes are often clustered in high-poverty neighborhoods, where disinvestment and poor housing conditions expose residents to triggers.
2382.name: Asthma hospitalizations (adults)

2383.description: Emergency department visits for asthma. Things like smoke, air pollution, dust mites, cockroaches, mold, pollen and pet dander can trigger asthma.
2383.name: Asthma emergency department visits (age 5 to 17), by NTA

2384.description: Emergency department visits for asthma. Things like smoke, air pollution, dust mites, cockroaches, mold, pollen and pet dander can trigger asthma.
2384.name: Asthma emergency department visits (adults), by NTA

2385.description: Hospitalizations for asthma. These more severe asthma outcomes are often clustered in high-poverty neighborhoods, where disinvestment and poor housing conditions expose residents to triggers.
2385.name: Asthma hospitalizations (age 4 and under), by NTA

2386.description: Hospitalizations for asthma. These more severe asthma outcomes are often clustered in high-poverty neighborhoods, where disinvestment and poor housing conditions expose residents to triggers.
2386.name: Asthma hospitalizations (age 5 to 17), by NTA

2387.description: Hospitalizations for asthma. These more severe asthma outcomes are often clustered in high-poverty neighborhoods, where disinvestment and poor housing conditions expose residents to triggers.
2387.name: Asthma hospitalizations (adults), by NTA

2388.description: The percentage of the population who live within walking distance to a park: a quarter-mile or less to entrances of smaller sites, such as sitting areas and playgrounds, and half-mile or less to entrances of larger parks. Increased access to green space and open space can contribute to increased levels of physical activity.
2388.name: Walking distance to a park

2389.description: The ratio of bodegas to supermarkets. This can indicate whether the environment makes accessing unhealthy food easier for residents, as bodegas are less likely to have healthy food options than supermarkets.
2389.name: Unhealthy food access

2390.description: Percent of street milage with bike lanes. Bike lanes can improve bicyclist and pedestrian safety, physical activity, and sustainable transportation use.
2390.name: Bicycle network coverage

2391.description: The percentage of population within a quarter-mile of a subway station entrance. When more people have convenient access to the transit system, they're more likely to use it. Subway access encourages active transportation, which improves the health of residents.
2391.name: Walking distance to a subway station

2392.description: Children ages 1 to 13 that have ever received an asthma diagnosis.
2392.name: Children ever diagnosed with asthma

2393.description: Children living in homes with reported cockroaches. The saliva, feces, and shedding body parts of cockroaches are an allergen and can trigger asthma.
2393.name: Children in homes with cockroaches (age 1-13)

2394.description: Children living in homes with reported mice. The presence of mice is associated with poor housing maintenance. Mice can contaminate food and worsen asthma.
2394.name: Children in homes with mice (age 1-13)

2395.description: Children living in homes with cracks or holes in walls, ceilings, or floors. This housing problem is linked to the presence of pets, which contaminate food and worsen asthma.
2395.name: Children in homes with cracks or holes (age 1-13)

2396.description: Children living in homes that use supplemental heat. This housing problem can indicate the presence of other health-threatening housing problems that can harm children's health.
2396.name: Children in homes with supplemental heat (age 13 and under)

2398.description: Deaths due to carbon monoxide. These may be fire-related or non-fire-related.
2398.name: Carbon monoxide deaths

2399.description: Renter-occupied homes with any health-related housing problems. Homes with housing problems can threaten the health of the people who live there.
2399.name: Renter-occupied homes with any health-related housing problems

24.description: Mice and rats are a source of household allergens connected to developing or worsening asthma.
24.name: Adults reporting mice or rats outside

2400.description: Non-fatal, violence-related injuries that result in emergency department visits. These are more common than homicides and help paint the larger picture of the burden of violence on communities.
2400.name: Violence-related emergency department visits (all ages)

2401.description: Households that postponed health care in the last 12 months
2401.name: Postponing health care

2404.description: The number of children aged 1-13 years exposed to tobacco smoke at home. Secondhand smoke is harmful to children and can cause or worsen respiratory and asthma issues and ear infections.
2404.name: Secondhand smoke exposure at home (children)

2405.description: Emergency department visits due to carbon monoxide. Carbon monoxide (CO) exposure can be life-threatening or fatal.
2405.name: Carbon monoxide emergency department visits

2406.description: Hospitalizations s due to carbon monoxide. Carbon monoxide (CO) exposure can be life-threatening or fatal.
2406.name: Carbon monoxide hospitalizations

2408.description: Emergency department visits due to home falls (age 65+). Falls are a leading cause of injury among older adults
2408.name: Home fall-related emergency department visits (age 65+)

2409.description: Hospitalizations due to home falls (age 65+). Falls are a leading cause of injury among older adults
2409.name: Home fall-related hospitalizations (age 65+)

2410.description: Hospitalizations due to hot weather. These are part of the public health burden due to hot weather. Data aggregated over 10 years provides enough stablility to display neighborhood impacts.
2410.name: Heat stress: 10-year hospitalizations

2411.description: The risk of community-level heat impacts, like deaths, due to extreme heat events. The HVI is made up of data on surface temperature, green space, air conditioning access, median income, and Black population (the population most excluded from heat resources). Differences in community-level heat impacts stem from structural racism, which limits access to preventive resources.
2411.name: Heat vulnerability index (NTA)

2414.description: Adults age 18 and older who have ever been diagnosed with asthma.
2414.name: Adults with asthma

2415.description: How adults commute to work, by mode: public transit, biking, walking, or private vehicles. People's means of transportation to work can shed light on transportation availability, choices, traffic levels, and safety.
2415.name: Commuting modes

2416.description: Public litter baskets (trash cans). Litter baskets are associated with a decrease in littering. Enclosed, non-wire baskets are generally better than wire baskets. Sanitation supports public health by providing clean, healthy public spaces for people to live, work, and get around.
2416.name: Litter basket coverage

2417.description: Adults who had depression. Depression is a common mental health condition that is characterized by feelings of sadness, difficulty concentrating, tiredness or reduced energy, and loss of interest in activities that used to bring enjoyment.
2417.name: Depression (adults)

2418.description: Adults hospitalized for a mental health-related reason. A  psychiatric hospitalization is an overnight stay or longer in a psychiatric inpatient unit (excluding emergency room visits without an inpatient admission) for individuals with behaviors or symptoms that are likely to result in harm to themselves or others.
2418.name: Psychiatric hospitalizations (adults)

2419.description: Adults with serious psychological distress (SPD). Serious psychological distress (SPD) is having problems functioning due to negative emotional or mental experiences.
2419.name: Serious psychological distress (adults)

2421.description: Retail locations that sell tobacco products. Neighborhoods with higher densities of tobacco retailers increase access to tobacco and may increase smoking rates.
2421.name: Tobacco retailers

2422.description: The number of children aged 1-13 years exposed to e-cigarette smoke at home all of the time, most of the time, or occasionally. Chemicals in the vapor from e-cigarettes can be harmful to kids.
2422.name: E-cigarette vapor exposure at home (children)

2425.description: The average number of Citi Bikes available to rent per each area between 7am-7pm. Biking bridges gaps in existing public transportation systems and is a great way to exercise. Neighborhoods with lower Citi Bike availability have limited access to this beneficial public resource.
2425.name: Average Citi Bike availability

2426.description: Biking bridges gaps in existing public transportation systems and is a great way to exercise. Neighborhoods with fewer Citi Bike stations have limited access to this beneficial public resource. Neighborhoods with relatively few docks per station may also have limited access to bikes even if they have many stations. The National Association of City Transportation Officials (NACTO) suggests that there should be 28 stations per square mile and one station every 1000 feet.
2426.name: Citi Bike stations

2427.description: Concentration of bacteria in waterways. Fecal coliform and enterococci are human-health-related indicators of water quality. Fecal coliform bacteria are found in human and animal intestines and are associated with wastewater. Enterococci may be a better indicator of wastewater pollution in a saltwater environment.
2427.name: Bacteria

2428.description: Dissolved oxygen in waterways. Ozygen is essential for most aquatic life. It is an important indicator of overall water quality.
2428.name: Dissolved oxygen (DO)

2429.description: Children ages 1 to 13 who have had an asthma attack in the past 12 months from when they were surveyed. Asthma attacks are a measurable adverse health outcome of asthma.
2429.name: Children with a recent asthma attack

2430.description: Children who live in homes with visible mold/mildew. Mold and mildew can trigger asthma attacks in children.
2430.name: Children in homes with visible mold or mildew (age 1-13)

2431.description: Children ages 1 to 13 that currently have asthma. Not every asthma diagnosis is correct. The number of children who still have asthma is usually smaller than the number of children who have ever been diagnosed with asthma.
2431.name: Children still with asthma

2432.description: Farmers' markets that are open at any point in the year. Farmers' markets are a source of fresh produce and other healthy food options and can help relieve the effects of food deserts.
2432.name: Farmers markets

2433.description: Rat indexing is a comprehensive approach for rat mitigation. In certain zones, every property is inspected every six months for signs of rats and the conditions that attract them.
2433.name: Rat indexing in Rat Mitigation Zones (RMZs)

2434.description: Rat inspections are conducted for signs of rats and the conditions that attract them.
2434.name: Rat inspections

2435.description: Non-fatal, violence-related injuries that result in emergency department visits. These are more common than homicides and help paint the larger picture of the burden of violence on communities.
2435.name: Violence-related emergency department visits (ages 15-34)

2436.description: Non-fatal injuries from firearms that result in emergency department visits. Violence from firearms causes physical and emotional harm, and trauma to both individuals and communities.
2436.name: Firearm emergency department visits (ages 15-34)

2437.description: Non-fatal injuries from firearms that result in emergency department visits. Violence from firearms causes physical and emotional harm, and trauma to both individuals and communities.
2437.name: Firearm emergency department visits (all ages)

2438.description: Non-fatal, violence-related injuries that result in hospitalizations. These are more common than homicides and help paint the larger picture of the burden of violence on communities.
2438.name: Violence-related hospitalizations (ages 15-34)

2439.description: Non-fatal injuries from firearms that result in hospitalizations. Violence from firearms causes physical and emotional harm, and trauma to both individuals and communities.
2439.name: Firearm hospitalizations (ages 15-34)

2440.description: Non-fatal injuries from firearms that result in hospitalizations. Violence from firearms causes physical and emotional harm, and trauma to both individuals and communities.
2440.name: Firearm hospitalizations (all ages)

2441.description: Cases of anaplasmosis. Anaplasmosis is a tick-borne disease transmitted through the bite of an infected blacklegged tick. Symptoms include fever, chills, headache, muscle aches, and fatigue. The majority of cases report a history of travel and outdoor exposures outside of NYC.
2441.name: Anaplasmosis

2442.description: Cases of Lyme disease. Lyme disease is transmitted through the bite of an infected blacklegged tick and is the most common tick-borne disease among New Yorkers. If left untreated, infection can spread to joints, the heart, and the nervous system. Most people acquire this disease while traveling outside NYC. In 2022, an expected increase in cases was observed due to changes in the case definition.
2442.name: Lyme disease

2443.description: ED visits due to heat-related illnesses, such as heat stroke and heat exhaustion. These are part of the public health burden of extreme heat.
2443.name: Heat stress: 5-year emergency department visits

2444.description: ED visits for cold-related illnesses, such as hypothermia and frostbite. These are part of the public health burden of cold weather. Cold weather can also make chronic conditions worse.
2444.name: Cold stress: 5-year emergency department visits

2445.description: Hospitalizations for cold-related illnesses, such as hypothermia and frostbite. These are part of the public health burden of cold weather. Cold weather can also make chronic conditions worse.
2445.name: Cold stress: 5-year hospitalizations

2446.description: Households reporting visible mold in the home. Mold can worsen respiratory conditions like asthma, and indicate maintenance problems in a building.
2446.name: Homes with mold

2447.description: Households reporting mice or rats in their unit or building. The presence of mice or rats in the home is often associated with poor housing maintenance. These pests can contaminate food and worsen asthma.
2447.name: Homes with mice or rats in the unit or building

2449.description: Concentration of fine particles in the air. Fine particles are emitted by vehicles, building boilers, and other combustion - and are a major form of air pollution that harms health. Regulatory PM2.5 sensors collect readings on the tops of buildings that measure regional changes in air quality for the federal Clean Air Act. This indicator is one of the federal standards for PM2.5 (9.0 µg/m3).
2449.name: Regulatory PM2.5 monitoring

2455.description: Accessible subway stations may include ramps, elevators, audio and visual information, or other access improvements, which can help New Yorkers with disabilities, those traveling with strollers, and older people use public transit more safely and reliably. Accessible infrastructure ensures that subway stations follow American Disabilities Act (ADA) guidelines.
2455.name: Accessible subway stations

2456.description: Bus stops equipped with button-activated audio announcements provide real-time bus arrival information for people who are blind or visually impaired.
2456.name: Bus stops with audio announcements

2457.description: Public bathrooms that are in service and open during scheduled hours. Public bathrooms help everyone take part in public life and make the city more livable for all New Yorkers.
2457.name: Public bathroom availability

2458.description: Population within a half mile of an accessible subway station. When more people have convenient access to the transit system, they're more likely to use it. Accessible subway stations may include ramps, elevators, or other access improvements that help New Yorkers with disabilities, those traveling with strollers, and older adults use public transit more safely and reliably. Accessible infrastructure ensures that subway stations follow American Disabilities Act (ADA) guidelines.
2458.name: Walking distance to an accessible subway station

2459.description: People with disabilities or access needs that make it difficult to walk or climb stairs. When transit and buildings have more accessible infrastructure like elevators and ramps it can make NYC easier to navigate for all New Yorkers. People with ambulatory difficulties may also need accommodation to navigate their home.
2459.name: Difficulty walking

2460.description: Population within a half mile of an accessible subway station. Bus stops equipped with button-activated audio announcements provide real-time bus arrival information for people who are blind or visually impaired.
2460.name: Walking distance to an audio bus stop

2461.description: People reporting trouble remembering, concentrating, or making decisions. Individuals with this difficulty may have access needs or benefit from accommodations.
2461.name: Cognitive difficulty

2462.description: People reporting serious trouble hearing. Individuals with trouble hearing may have access needs or benefit from accommodations.
2462.name: Hearing difficulty

2463.description: People reporting trouble practicing self-care. These individuals have trouble with essential self-care activities such as bathing, dressing, and getting around their residence. They may benefit from assistance or accommodations.
2463.name: Self-care difficulty

2464.description: People reporting blindness or serious trouble seeing (even when wearing glasses). These individuals may have access needs or benefit from accommodations.
2464.name: Vision difficulty

25.description: Adults reporting secondhand smoke at home. Secondhand smoke, especially indoors, is bad for health - particularly for the health of children.
25.name: Secondhand smoke at home

26.description: A serious birth defect in which a baby is born without parts of the brain and skull.
26.name: Anencephaly

27.description: A neural tube defect that can cause cause physical and intellectual disabilities.
27.name: Spina bifida (without anencephaly)

28.description: A rare birth defect where part of the heart is underdeveloped.
28.name: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome

29.description: A congenital heart defect that involves abnormal arrangement of parts of the heart.
29.name: Transposition of the great arteries (vessels)

30.description: A birth defect that occurs when a baby's lip does not form properly during pregnancy.
30.name: Cleft lip (with or without cleft palate)

31.description: A birth defect that occurs when a baby's mouth does not form properly during pregnancy.
31.name: Cleft palate (without cleft lip)

32.description: A birth defect in male babies where the urethra opening is not at the tip of the penis.
32.name: Hypospadias

33.description: A birth defect where there is a hole beside the belly button and the baby's intestines or other organs are outside the baby's body.
33.name: Gastroschisis

34.description: Undergrowth, overgrowth, failure of formation, and other variations or deficiencies in the upper limbs.
34.name: Upper limb deficiencies

35.description: Undergrowth, overgrowth, failure of formation, and other variations or deficiencies in the lower limbs.
35.name: Lower limb Deficiencies

36.description: A condition in which a person has an extra chromosome. It causes delays in physical growth, and intellectual disabilities.
36.name: Down syndrome (mother under age 35)

37.description: A condition in which a person has an extra chromosome. It causes delays in physical growth, and intellectual disabilities.
37.name: Down syndrome (mother age 35+)

38.description: A leak where the Fire Department measures at least 1 ppm of carbon monixide at the scene.
38.name: Carbon monoxide incidents

4.description: Birth weight under 5 pounds, 8 ounces at full term.
4.name: Low birthweight at full term

40.description: Households reporting cracks or holes in the home. This maintenance problem is linked to mice, rats, and cockroaches - which can harm residents' health.
40.name: Homes with cracks or holes

41.description: Housing built before 1960 with peeling paint. This can put residents at risk of lead poisoning. Lead paint was banned from household paints in New York City in 1960 and in the USA in 1978.
41.name: Old homes with peeling paint

42.description: Households reporting leaks from outside the unit. This maintenance problem can introduce mold, which can worsen respiratory conditions like asthma.
42.name: Homes with leaks

45.description: Households reporting 3 or more housing problems. These can threaten the health of the people who live there.
45.name: Homes with 3+ housing problems

46.description: Building quality predicts the number of housing maintenance problems in a residence that place residents at increased risk of acute or chronic health problems.
46.name: Homes near structures rated good or excellent

47.description: Households using supplemental heat, like a space heater. This may mean a building's main heat source doesn't work. It can indicate the presence of other health-threatening maintenance deficiencies, and increase fire risk.
47.name: Homes using supplemental heat

48.description: Households reporting mice or rats in their building in the past 90 days (from when they were surveyed). The presence of rodents is associated with housing problems. These pests can contaminate food and worsen asthma.
48.name: Homes with mice or rats in the building

5.description: Death among children under 1 year old.
5.name: Death (infants)

55.description: Days when ozone levels are at unhealthy levels. Ozone is a common air pollutant that can harm breathing and worsen asthma and other respiratory conditions. Ozone action days are when the AQI is above 100, mainly due to ozone.
55.name: Ozone action days

57.description: Days when PM2.5 is at an unhealthy level. PM2.5 is emitted by combustion and are a major form of air pollution that harms health. PM2.5 action days are when the AQI is above 100, mainly due to PM2.5
57.name: Fine particles (PM 2.5) action days

6.description: Deaths among children less than 28 days old.
6.name: Death (neonatal)

60.description: Breast cancer is a common cancer. It is more common among females.
60.name: Breast cancer (in females)

63.description: Cancers in the lung or bronchus.
63.name: Lung and bronchus cancer

66.description: Brain and other nervous system cancers are tumors that start in the brain or spinal cord.
66.name: Brain and other nervous system cancer

690.description: Cancer of the thyroid, a gland in the neck.
690.name: Thyroid cancer

7.description: Deaths from 28 weeks of pregnancy to 6 days old.
7.name: Death (perinatal)

71.description: A cancer that starts in the lymphatic system, part of the body's immune system.
71.name: Non-Hodgkin's lymphomas

73.description: Leukemia is a general term for cancer of blood cells.
73.name: Leukemia

74.description: Acute myeloid leukemia is a cancer of the blood and bone marrow.
74.name: Acute myeloid leukemia

770.description: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is a cancer that starts from white blood cells in bone marrow.
770.name: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia

8.description: Deaths from 28 days old to 1 year old.
8.name: Death (postneonatal)

84.description: Asthma hospitalizations are more severe asthma outcomes. They're often clustered in high-poverty neighborhoods, where disinvestment and poor housing conditions expose residents to triggers.
84.name: Asthma hospitalizations (age 4 and under)

91.description: Households that report using a regular exterminator service.
91.name: Regular exterminator service

92.description: Days when air quality is unhealthy. Action days for sensitive groups are counted when either ozone or PM2.5 levels are above 100, and for the general population when levels are above 150.
92.name: Air quality action days

93.description: Pesticides targeting insects, applied by professional exterminators or licensed maintenance staff.
93.name: Commercial use of insecticides

94.description: Pesticides targeting unwanted weeds, grasses, vines and trees applied by professional exterminators or licensed maintenance staff.
94.name: Commercial use of herbicides

96.description: Pesticides targeting type of fungus such as mold or plant blight applied by professional exterminators or licensed maintenance staff. These are often applied to protect landscaping and golf course grasses.
96.name: Commercial use of fungicides

97.description: Pesticides of this chemical class used to target insects, applied by professional exterminators or licensed maintenance staff. Organophosphates are acutely toxic and present a significant health risk from human exposure.
97.name: Commercial use of insecticides (Organophosphate)

98.description: Pyrethroids and Pyrethrins are less acutely toxic than some other insecticide classes. But based on how they are broadly applied, they can present a significant risk of human exposure. These chemicals can also cause a respiratory allergic reaction and short term irritation to the skin and face.
98.name: Commercial use of insecticides (Pyrethroid/Pyrethrin)

99.description: Carbamates are acutely toxic and present a significant health risk from human exposure.
99.name: Commercial use of insecticides (Carbamate)
